attempts.text: When a language model is used to evaluate answers, the evaluator itself becomes an object of assessment. Multilingual studies already examine this problem. Fu and Liu evaluate judgments on parallel language versions, and Chung and Freienthal investigate cross-language stability in controlled customer-support dialogues. Their work gives direct precedents for studying language-dependent evaluation; it does not support a claim that multilingual judging has been overlooked. [[S01]]; [[S02]].
